title: Taj Mahal Visit Guide: Tickets, Timings, Friday Closure & Best Time
quickAnswer: Open every day except Friday, from about 30 minutes before sunrise. Entry is ₹50 for Indians and ₹1,100 for most foreign visitors, plus ₹200 for the main mausoleum. Under-15s enter free. Book online and arrive at opening time.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Taj Mahal Tickets, Timings & Friday Closure (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Taj Mahal ticket prices, opening hours, the Friday closure, night viewing and the best time to visit, checked against official sources.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day Agra plan that avoids Fridays and starts at opening time.

ogTitle: Taj Mahal Visit Guide: Tickets, Timings, Friday Closure & Best Time
ogDescription: Taj Mahal ticket prices, opening hours, the Friday closure, night viewing and the best time to visit, checked against official sources.
content:
The Taj Mahal is open every day except Friday, from about 30 minutes before sunrise. Entry costs ₹50 for Indian citizens and ₹1,100 for most foreign visitors, plus an optional ₹200 to go inside the main mausoleum. Children under 15 enter free. Book online, arrive at opening time, and keep Friday for something else.

Most people get the big picture right and the small details wrong: they turn up on a Friday, queue for a ticket that is cheaper online, or reach the gate at 11 am with half of Agra. This guide covers the details that decide whether your visit is calm or crowded.

{{fig:facts}}

Taj Mahal ticket prices

Prices are set by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Agra Development Authority. The table shows the published amounts at the time of writing.

VisitorComplex entryMain mausoleum (optional)Total
Indian citizens and OCI cardholders₹50+ ₹200₹250
SAARC and BIMSTEC nationals₹540+ ₹200₹740
Other foreign nationals₹1,100+ ₹200₹1,300
Children under 15FreeFreeFree

Buying online saves ₹5 on each Indian ticket and ₹50 on each foreign ticket, according to the official Taj Mahal website. More useful than the saving: an online ticket lets you skip the ticket counter queue and walk straight to security.

Is the mausoleum ticket worth it?

For a first visit, yes. The ₹200 ticket takes you inside the white marble chamber with the cenotaphs of Mumtaz Mahal and Shah Jahan. It is dim, crowded and photography is not allowed inside, so it takes ten minutes, not an hour. If you are short on time or travelling with small children, the gardens and outer platform are the main experience anyway.

Opening hours and the Friday closure

The Taj opens about 30 minutes before sunrise and closes around sunset, so the exact time shifts through the year. It is closed to sightseers every Friday, when the mosque inside the complex is used for prayers. Plan your Agra day for any other day of the week, and if you arrive on a Thursday night, make sure Friday has a different plan, such as Fatehpur Sikri.

The best time to visit

  • At opening time: the gates fill fast. Being in the first group through security gives you the reflecting pools with fewer people in the frame and softer light on the marble.
  • October to March: the most comfortable months. December and January mornings can be foggy, so the dome may appear slowly. That is part of the charm, but do not plan your only photo slot for 7 am in January.
  • Avoid late morning in summer: from April to June, white marble under midday sun is hard on the eyes and feet.
{{photo:mehtab-bagh}}

Sunset from across the river

You cannot stay inside after closing, but you can watch sunset from Mehtab Bagh, the Mughal garden on the opposite bank of the Yamuna. It is aligned with the Taj, quieter than the main complex and needs a separate ticket. Pair it with a morning at the Taj and an afternoon at Agra Fort, which has its own separate ticket too.

Night viewing

Night viewing runs on a few nights around the full moon each month (not on Fridays), in small timed batches. Tickets are limited and sold in advance through the ASI. It is a quiet, distant view rather than a close-up, so treat it as a bonus, not a replacement for a daytime visit.

{{fig:checklist}}

What you can and cannot carry

Security is airport-style. Keep it simple: phone, wallet, ID, a small bottle of water and your camera. Food, tobacco, large bags and tripods are not allowed, and there is no point carrying them to the gate. Drones are banned. Shoe covers are provided for the mausoleum platform, so you do not need to remove shoes.

How to get there and how long to spend

Agra is an easy day trip from Delhi by train. The fastest trains, such as the Gatimaan Express and Vande Bharat, take about 1 hour 40 minutes to Agra Cantt. By road it is about 230 km on the Yamuna Expressway. Inside the complex, allow two to three hours, plus queue time.

A same-day trip is possible, but an overnight in Agra lets you take the sunrise slot without a 4 am start from Delhi. Our 2-day Agra itinerary does exactly that, and the 5-day Golden Triangle plan fits Agra between Delhi and Jaipur.

Quick answers

Is the Taj Mahal open on Sunday?

Yes. It is open every day except Friday.

Do children need a ticket?

Children under 15 enter free, but they still go through security with you.

Can I buy tickets at the gate?

Yes, but buying online is cheaper and quicker. Use the official ASI booking linked from the Taj Mahal website rather than third-party resellers.

Ticket prices and hours were checked against official sources in November 2026. Fees can change, so confirm on the official site before you go.

facts.alt: Taj Mahal at a glance: Open: Sat–Thu, from ~30 min before sunrise; Closed: Every Friday; Indians: ₹50 + ₹200 mausoleum; Foreign visitors: ₹1,100 + ₹200 mausoleum; Children: Under 15 free; Time needed: 2–3 hours + queue
facts.caption: Taj Mahal at a glance. Checked November 2026.

checklist.alt: Before you go: 1. Check your Agra day is not a Friday; 2. Book online: cheaper, no ticket queue; 3. Be at the gate at opening time; 4. Carry ID; no food, tripods or drones; 5. Add the ₹200 mausoleum ticket for a first visit; 6. Sunset? Go to Mehtab Bagh across the river
checklist.caption: Before you go.

title: Manali in Winter: Where to Find Snow, Atal Tunnel & Rohtang Closure
quickAnswer: You can see snow around Manali in winter, but not at Rohtang Pass, which is closed to tourists through the snow season and usually reopens in May. Plan on Solang Valley, and the Atal Tunnel and Sissu on days the police allow tourist traffic.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Manali in Winter: Snow, Atal Tunnel & Rohtang (2026)
metaDescription: Where to see snow in Manali in winter, when Rohtang Pass is closed, how the Atal Tunnel and Sissu work in snow, and a 3-day plan that still works.

cta.ctaBody: Get a flexible day-by-day plan with a backup for closed roads.

ogTitle: Manali in Winter: Where to Find Snow, Atal Tunnel & Rohtang Closure
ogDescription: Where to see snow in Manali in winter, when Rohtang Pass is closed, how the Atal Tunnel and Sissu work in snow, and a 3-day plan that still works.
content:
Yes, you can see snow in Manali in winter, but not at Rohtang Pass. Rohtang closes to tourists once heavy snow arrives (usually by December) and normally reopens in May. Your realistic snow plan is Solang Valley, and the Atal Tunnel and Sissu on the days the police allow tourist traffic through.

Winter Manali rewards travellers who stay flexible. One snowfall can open up postcard views and close the road you planned to drive the next morning. This guide sets your expectations by month and gives you a plan that still works when the roads do not.

{{fig:facts}}

When does it snow in Manali?

Snow in Manali town is never guaranteed, even in January. Higher spots around it see snow far more reliably:

  • December: cold, clear days with occasional early snowfall. Snow is most likely at Solang and higher up.
  • January and February: the heaviest snow months. This is the best chance of snow everywhere, and also when roads close most often.
  • March: snow still lingers higher up, the days get warmer and roads reopen more steadily.

Plan for snow you can drive to, not snow outside your window. If fresh snowfall in town matters to you, keep two or three flexible days instead of a tight schedule.

Rohtang Pass in winter: closed

Rohtang Pass is shut to tourists through the main snow season. In January 2026, for example, the highway was closed beyond Gulaba after fresh snow and black ice, and Rohtang reopened for the 2026 season in mid-May. When it is open, it needs an online permit and is closed on Tuesdays for maintenance. In winter, simply leave it out of your plans.

{{photo:atal-tunnel}}

Atal Tunnel and Sissu: the winter alternative

The Atal Tunnel runs under the Rohtang ridge to Sissu in Lahaul. It is about 38–40 km from Manali through Solang, roughly 1 to 1.5 hours in clear conditions. No permit is needed for the tunnel itself.

Here is the catch most guides skip: the tunnel road is not always open to tourists in winter. After heavy snowfall the police stop tourist vehicles at Solang or earlier, sometimes for days. In January 2026, the road to the tunnel was blocked by snow for stretches and later opened only for local 4x4 vehicles with chains. Check with your hotel or driver the evening before, and never push past a police barrier.

Solang Valley: the most reliable snow day

Solang Valley, about 14 km from Manali, is where most winter visitors play in the snow: snow tubing, skiing lessons for beginners, and the ropeway when it is running. On the busiest days the last stretch can jam, so leave early.

{{fig:checklist}}

Getting there in winter

  • By air: the nearest airport is Bhuntar (Kullu), about 50 km away. Winter flights are few and weather delays are common.
  • By overnight bus: Volvo buses from Delhi are the most popular option. They usually stop in the town or at the outskirts depending on conditions.
  • By car: the road via Mandi and Kullu stays open in winter, but carry chains if you plan to drive beyond Manali after snowfall, and avoid driving after dark.

A sensible 3-day winter plan

  1. Day 1: arrive, rest, and walk Old Manali and Hadimba Temple in the cedar forest.
  2. Day 2: Solang Valley for snow activities, early start.
  3. Day 3: Atal Tunnel and Sissu if the road is open. If it is closed, swap in Naggar Castle and the Kullu valley.

Our 3-day Manali itinerary and 4-day version give the full day-by-day plan, with timings.

What to pack

Thermals, a down jacket, waterproof gloves and boots with good grip matter more than anything else. Hotels in winter often rely on room heaters, so ask before booking whether heating is included.

Road and pass information reflects official and news reports checked in November 2026. Winter road status changes daily. Confirm locally before driving beyond Manali.

facts.alt: Manali in winter: what's open: Rohtang Pass: Closed in winter, usually reopens in May; Atal Tunnel: No permit; closes after heavy snow; Manali → Sissu: ~38–40 km, 1–1.5 hrs when open; Solang Valley: ~14 km; most reliable snow day; Heaviest snow: January–February; Nearest airport: Bhuntar (Kullu), ~50 km
facts.caption: Manali in winter: what's open. Checked November 2026.

checklist.alt: Winter road checklist: 1. Keep 2–3 flexible days for snow; 2. Check Atal Tunnel status the evening before; 3. Never cross a police barrier; 4. Leave early for Solang to beat jams; 5. Pack thermals, waterproof gloves, grippy boots; 6. Ask hotels if heating is included
checklist.caption: Winter road checklist.

title: Gulmarg in Winter: Gondola Phases, Booking, Skiing & Snow Guide
quickAnswer: Gulmarg is best from late December to March. The two-stage gondola runs to Kongdoori (about 3,050 m) and then Apharwat (about 3,980 m). Book both phases online in advance, take an early slot, and stay at least one night.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Gulmarg in Winter: Gondola Booking, Skiing & Snow
metaDescription: How the Gulmarg Gondola's two phases work, how to book, why Phase 2 closes, skiing for beginners and how to plan Gulmarg from Srinagar in winter.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day Srinagar and Gulmarg plan built around gondola timings.

ogTitle: Gulmarg in Winter: Gondola Phases, Booking, Skiing & Snow Guide
ogDescription: How the Gulmarg Gondola's two phases work, how to book, why Phase 2 closes, skiing for beginners and how to plan Gulmarg from Srinagar in winter.
content:
Gulmarg is at its best from late December to March, when the meadow turns into one of India's main ski areas. The highlight is the two-stage Gulmarg Gondola: Phase 1 climbs to Kongdoori (about 3,050 m) and Phase 2 continues to Apharwat (about 3,980 m). Book both phases online in advance, and plan to arrive at your time slot early.

Most first-time visitors come for a day from Srinagar, ride the gondola and leave. That works, but Gulmarg in winter is better with at least one night, so you can catch the first slot of the morning, before the queue and before the clouds roll in.

{{fig:facts}}

The Gulmarg Gondola, explained

The gondola is run by the Jammu & Kashmir Cable Car Corporation. It has two separate stages, and the second is the one most people really want:

  • Phase 1: Gulmarg to Kongdoori. A short ride to a snowy bowl with sledges, snow play and views back over the meadow. Reported fare about ₹810 per person.
  • Phase 2: Kongdoori to Apharwat. It climbs close to 4,000 m into deep snow, ski runs and big Himalayan views. Reported fare about ₹1,010 per person.

Booking guides report that you need a Phase 1 booking before you can book Phase 2, and Phase 2 sells fewer seats a day. So book both together, two or three days ahead in peak season. Fares change, so check the official portal when you book rather than relying on a number from a blog, including this one.

{{fig:checklist}}

Why Phase 2 closes so often

Phase 2 stops in high wind, heavy snowfall and poor visibility, and it often runs only in the morning on stormy days. That is why the first slot of the day matters. If Phase 2 is shut, Phase 1 alone is still a good snow day. Ask at the counter what the operator's current refund or reschedule rules are, and keep your booking reference handy.

Skiing in Gulmarg

Gulmarg has gentle beginner slopes near the base and serious off-piste terrain from Apharwat. Beginners can hire skis and an instructor for half a day at the base. Experienced skiers come for the powder on the upper mountain, ideally with a local guide, because avalanche risk is real after fresh snowfall.

Getting there

Gulmarg is about 50 km from Srinagar, roughly 1.5 to 2 hours by road in winter. Taxis from Srinagar are the usual way up. After heavy snow, the last stretch from Tanmarg can need chains or a 4x4, and the police sometimes hold traffic until the road is cleared.

Fly into Srinagar, spend a night or two there for the old city and a shikara on Dal Lake, then head up. Our 2-day Gulmarg itinerary covers the gondola timing, and the 5-day Srinagar, Gulmarg and Pahalgam plan fits it into a wider Kashmir trip.

{{photo:dal-lake}}

How cold is it?

Very. Nights are well below freezing from December to February, and Apharwat is much colder than the base, with wind chill. Wear proper layers, waterproof boots and gloves, and sunglasses for the glare. Hired snow boots and jackets are available near the gondola base, but the fit and quality vary.

Common mistakes

  • Booking Phase 1 only and hoping to add Phase 2 at the top. There is no ticket counter at Kongdoori.
  • Planning the gondola for the afternoon, when wind and cloud are most likely to stop Phase 2.
  • Paying touts for "guaranteed" tickets. Book on the official portal.

Fares and booking rules are as reported in November 2026. Confirm on the official J&K Cable Car Corporation portal before you travel.

facts.alt: Gulmarg Gondola at a glance: Phase 1: Gulmarg → Kongdoori, ~3,050 m; Phase 2: Kongdoori → Apharwat, ~3,980 m; Phase 1 fare: ~₹810 reported; check portal; Phase 2 fare: ~₹1,010 reported; check portal; Booking: Online, Phase 1 before Phase 2; Best season: Late December to March
facts.caption: Gulmarg Gondola at a glance. Checked November 2026.

checklist.alt: Gondola day checklist: 1. Book both phases together, 2–3 days ahead; 2. Take the earliest slot you can get; 3. Expect Phase 2 to stop in wind or storms; 4. Keep your booking reference handy; 5. Avoid touts selling 'guaranteed' tickets; 6. Wear waterproof boots, gloves, sunglasses
checklist.caption: Gondola day checklist.

title: Ladakh for First-Timers: Best Time, Acclimatisation & Permits (2026)
quickAnswer: Go between June and September, fly into Leh and rest for the first 48 hours, as the Ladakh administration advises. Indian travellers pay an environment fee online instead of the old Inner Line Permit; foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit for Nubra and Pangong.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Ladakh for First-Timers: Best Time, Altitude & Permits
metaDescription: When to visit Ladakh, why the first 48 hours in Leh matter, 2026 permit rules for Indians and foreigners, and a safe 7-day first route.

cta.ctaHeading: Plan a safe first Ladakh trip
cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day route with acclimatisation days built in.

ogTitle: Ladakh for First-Timers: Best Time, Acclimatisation & Permits (2026)
ogDescription: When to visit Ladakh, why the first 48 hours in Leh matter, 2026 permit rules for Indians and foreigners, and a safe 7-day first route.
content:
For a first trip, go to Ladakh between June and September, fly into Leh, and rest for the first 48 hours before going higher. The Ladakh administration's advisory asks for that 48-hour acclimatisation. Indian travellers pay an environment and development fee online instead of getting the old Inner Line Permit. Foreign nationals still need a Protected Area Permit for places like Nubra and Pangong.

Ladakh is not hard because of distances. It is hard because of altitude. Leh sits at about 3,500 m, and the passes you will cross on day trips go far higher. Plan around your body first and your sightseeing second, and the trip becomes much easier.

{{fig:facts}}

When to go

MonthsWhat to expectGood for
June to SeptemberRoads open, warm days, cold nights. Peak season.First-timers, road trips, lakes
May and OctoberFewer crowds. Passes may still have snow or start closing.Flexible travellers
November to AprilSevere cold. The highways from Manali and Srinagar are usually closed, so you can only fly in.Experienced winter travellers only

The two road routes are only open for part of the year. The Srinagar–Leh highway is usually open from about April or May, and the Manali–Leh highway from about May or June to September or October. In 2026, for example, the Manali–Leh road opened to light vehicles in mid-May.

The first 48 hours: do this properly

Most people fly in from Delhi in about 1 hour 20 minutes, which means going from near sea level to 3,500 m with no time to adjust. The official Ladakh Tourism advisory asks visitors to allow at least 48 hours to acclimatise in Leh, and Ladakh Police give the same advice.

{{fig:checklist}}

If you arrive by road from Srinagar, the gradual climb helps, but rest still matters. Headache, nausea, breathlessness at rest or confusion are warning signs. Do not go higher with them; see a doctor in Leh. Talk to your own doctor before the trip if you have heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions, or if you are considering preventive medicine.

Permits in 2026

  • Indian citizens: pay the Ladakh environment and development fee online on the official LAHDC Leh permit portal, then carry the receipt (printed or on your phone). It may be checked at checkposts on the way to Nubra, Pangong and other restricted areas.
  • Foreign nationals: need a Protected Area Permit for restricted areas such as Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso, usually arranged through a registered travel agent in Leh.

Fee amounts and the list of areas can change, so check the portal for current figures rather than trusting older blog numbers.

{{photo:pangong-tso}}

A first-timer's route

A balanced first trip is seven days. Keep two days in and around Leh to acclimatise, then visit Nubra over Khardung La, and Pangong over Chang La. Days 1 and 2 should be easy: Leh Palace, the market, and short drives to Thiksey or Hemis monasteries, which are lower than the passes.

Our 7-day Leh, Nubra and Pangong itinerary follows this pattern day by day. If you only have four days, the Leh and monasteries plan skips the high lakes and keeps you at a safer altitude.

Practical tips

  • Phones: coverage is patchy outside Leh. Download offline maps and tell someone your plan.
  • Cash: carry some. ATMs outside Leh are few.
  • Sun: the UV is strong even when the air is cold. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses and a hat.
  • Responsible travel: carry a refillable bottle and bring your rubbish back to Leh.

Advisories, permits and road seasons were checked against official and recent reports in November 2026. Check the official portals before you travel.

facts.alt: Ladakh essentials: Best months: June–September; Leh altitude: About 3,500 m; Acclimatise: At least 48 hours in Leh; Indians: Environment fee online, carry receipt; Foreign nationals: Protected Area Permit via agent; Roads: Usually closed Nov–Apr; fly in
facts.caption: Ladakh essentials. Checked November 2026.

checklist.alt: Your first 48 hours in Leh: 1. Rest on day 1: no sightseeing climbs; 2. Drink plenty of water; 3. No alcohol or smoking; 4. Only short, easy walks; 5. Lower monasteries before high passes; 6. Headache or breathless at rest? Don't go higher
checklist.caption: Your first 48 hours in Leh.

title: Havelock & Neil Ferry Guide: How to Plan the Andaman Islands
quickAnswer: Take a ferry from Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram): private catamarans like Makruzz, Nautika, Green Ocean and ITT Majestic take about 1.5–2.5 hours to Havelock, and Havelock to Neil is about an hour. Book private ferries online early; government ferries are cheaper but slower.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Havelock & Neil Ferry Guide: Andaman Islands Planning
metaDescription: How to plan Port Blair, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep) by ferry: operators, journey times, private vs government ferries and booking tips.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day island plan with ferries in the right order.

ogTitle: Havelock & Neil Ferry Guide: How to Plan the Andaman Islands
ogDescription: How to plan Port Blair, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep) by ferry: operators, journey times, private vs government ferries and booking tips.
content:
To reach Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep), you take a ferry from Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram). Private catamarans such as Makruzz, Nautika, Green Ocean and ITT Majestic take about 1.5 to 2.5 hours to Havelock, and Havelock to Neil is about an hour. Book private ferries online in advance. Government ferries are cheaper but slower, with limited and mostly counter-based booking.

Ferries are the backbone of an Andaman trip, and they decide your itinerary more than any beach does. Get the sequence and the timings right, and the islands feel easy. Get them wrong, and you lose a day sitting at a jetty.

{{fig:compare}}

The classic route

Most trips follow one loop: Port Blair → Havelock → Neil → Port Blair. You fly into Port Blair, take a morning ferry to Havelock, spend two or three nights there, hop to Neil for a night or two, and return to Port Blair a day before your flight out.

  • Port Blair to Havelock: about 1.5 to 2.5 hours, depending on the boat and the sea.
  • Havelock to Neil: about 1 to 1.5 hours.
  • Neil to Port Blair: roughly 1 to 1.5 hours on the faster boats.

Private vs government ferries

Private catamaransGovernment (DSS) ferries
OperatorsMakruzz, Nautika, Green Ocean, ITT MajesticDirectorate of Shipping Services
ComfortAir-conditioned, assigned seatsBasic seating, open deck
SpeedFastest optionSlower
BookingOnline, weeks ahead in peak seasonLimited, mostly at counters, short booking window
Best forShort trips and fixed plansBudget travellers with flexible dates

Schedules and fares change by season, and some operators run fewer sailings in the monsoon months. Check each operator's current timetable when you book rather than relying on an older list.

{{photo:shaheed-dweep}}

How many days on each island?

  • Havelock: 2–3 nights. Radhanagar Beach at sunset, a snorkelling or diving day, and Elephant Beach by boat.
  • Neil: 1–2 nights. Smaller and slower. Cycle between Bharatpur, Laxmanpur and Sitapur beaches.
  • Port Blair: 1–2 nights. Cellular Jail and its evening light-and-sound show, plus a buffer before your flight.

Our 4-day Havelock and Neil itinerary and the 5-day Andaman plan lay this out day by day.

{{fig:checklist}}

Ferry tips that save a day

  • Book the ferries before the hotels. Popular morning sailings fill first, and your hotel dates should follow your boat.
  • Do not take a ferry on your flight day. Weather can delay or cancel sailings. Spend your last night in Port Blair.
  • Report early. Arrive at the jetty about an hour before departure with photo ID matching your booking.
  • Pack light. Ferries have luggage limits, and jetties involve some walking.
  • Seasickness: morning sailings are often calmer. Take your usual remedy before boarding.

Best time to go

October to May is the main season, with calmer seas. The southwest monsoon, roughly June to September, brings rough water, fewer sailings and more cancellations. December and January are the busiest months, so book ferries as soon as your flights are fixed.

Operators, routes and journey times were checked against operator and booking-site information in November 2026. Timetables change by season. Confirm with the operator before booking.

Government (DSS) ferries: Run by the A&N administration; Basic seats, open deck; Slower crossings; Limited, mostly counter booking.

title: Kerala Houseboat Guide: Alleppey vs Kumarakom, Timings & Booking Tips
quickAnswer: Overnight houseboats usually board around noon and end around 9 am, with meals on board. Cruising stops at about 5:30 pm, when the boat anchors for the night. Choose Alleppey for more boats and canals, or Kumarakom for a quieter stay on Vembanad Lake.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Kerala Houseboat Guide: Alleppey vs Kumarakom & Timings
metaDescription: How an overnight Kerala houseboat works, why cruising stops at 5:30 pm, Alleppey vs Kumarakom, day vs overnight cruises and what to ask before you book.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day plan with Kochi, Munnar and the backwaters.

ogTitle: Kerala Houseboat Guide: Alleppey vs Kumarakom, Timings & Booking Tips
ogDescription: How an overnight Kerala houseboat works, why cruising stops at 5:30 pm, Alleppey vs Kumarakom, day vs overnight cruises and what to ask before you book.
content:
An overnight houseboat in Kerala usually boards around noon and ends around 9 am the next day, with all meals cooked on board. Cruising stops at about 5:30 pm, when the boat anchors for the night, so most of your actual cruising happens in the afternoon. Choose Alleppey (Alappuzha) for more boats and canal routes, or Kumarakom for a quieter stay on Vembanad Lake.

A houseboat is one of the few Indian travel experiences where doing nothing is the point. But the experience varies a lot from one boat to the next, and the brochures rarely mention the rules that shape your day. Here is what to know before you pay.

{{fig:compare}}

How an overnight cruise actually works

  1. Around noon: board at the jetty, with a welcome drink and a cabin check.
  2. Afternoon: cruise through the backwaters while lunch is cooked on board. Lunch is often served while the boat is moored.
  3. About 5:30 pm: the boat stops and anchors for the night. Cruising after dark is not allowed, partly so local fishermen can use the waterways at night.
  4. Evening: tea and snacks, a village walk if you are moored near one, then dinner on board.
  5. Next morning: a short cruise back after breakfast, with checkout around 9 to 9:30 am.

In practice, you get about 5 to 6 hours of cruising, spread over the afternoon and the next morning. If you want more time on the water and less in the cabin, a day cruise may suit you better.

Overnight or day cruise?

  • Overnight: the full experience, with the quiet evening, meals on board and sunrise on the water. Best for couples and families who want to slow down.
  • Day cruise: usually late morning to late afternoon, with lunch included. Best if you are short on time or unsure about sleeping on a boat.
{{photo:alleppey-backwater-houseboat-cruise}}

Alleppey or Kumarakom?

Alleppey has by far the most boats, the busiest jetties and the most variety, from basic one-bedroom boats to large luxury ones. Its narrow canals give you the village-life scenes most people imagine. Kumarakom, across Vembanad Lake, is quieter and more resort-based, with fewer boats and wider water. Choose Alleppey for choice and canal life, and Kumarakom for calm.

{{fig:checklist}}

Choosing a good boat

Two boats can look identical online and feel completely different on board. Before you pay, ask:

  • Is the boat registered and approved by Kerala Tourism? Ask for its classification and registration.
  • When is the air-conditioning on? On many boats it runs only at night, not all day.
  • What is the route? Ask whether it includes narrow canals or only the open lake.
  • What exactly is included in meals and drinks, and what costs extra?
  • Is the boat shared or private? Many "deluxe" boats have one to three cabins, so ask if you will share the deck.
  • What is the cancellation policy if heavy rain or a strike stops the cruise?

When to go

September to March is the most pleasant time, with cooler evenings after the monsoon. The monsoon, June to August, is lush and dramatic but wet, and some cruises shorten their routes. Weekends and the Christmas to New Year period are the busiest and most expensive.

Where it fits in a Kerala trip

Most travellers combine a houseboat with Kochi and the tea hills of Munnar. Alleppey is about 1.5 to 2 hours by road from Kochi. See our 5-day Kochi, Munnar and backwaters itinerary or the 6-day backwaters and tea hills plan, and our guide to the Alleppey houseboat cruise.

Cruise timings reflect standard operator practice, checked in November 2026. Individual boats vary, so confirm check-in, AC hours and route with your operator. For official information, see Kerala Tourism.

title: North Goa vs South Goa: Which Side Should You Stay On?
quickAnswer: Pick North Goa for busy beaches, nightlife, markets and food. Pick South Goa for wide, quieter beaches and slower, resort-style days. Fly into Mopa (GOX) for the north and Dabolim (GOI) for the south.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: North Goa vs South Goa: Where to Stay (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: North Goa or South Goa? Compare beaches, nightlife, crowds and stays, which airport to fly into, and how to combine both in one trip.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day Goa plan for the side that suits you.

ogTitle: North Goa vs South Goa: Which Side Should You Stay On?
ogDescription: North Goa or South Goa? Compare beaches, nightlife, crowds and stays, which airport to fly into, and how to combine both in one trip.
content:
Choose North Goa if you want busy beaches, nightlife, markets and lots of places to eat within a short ride. Choose South Goa if you want wide, quieter beaches, slower days and resort-style stays. Goa now has two airports: Mopa (GOX) in the north and Dabolim (GOI) further south, so pick your base first and book flights to the closer one.

Goa is a small state, but the north and south feel like different holidays. Most disappointing Goa trips come from staying on the wrong side: party-seekers stuck in a quiet south Goa resort, or couples looking for calm who end up on the Baga strip on a Saturday night.

{{fig:compare}}

North Goa: for energy and variety

The north is the Goa of postcards and parties: Calangute and Baga for crowds and water sports, Anjuna and Vagator for cafés, cliffs and the flea market, and Arambol and Mandrem further north for a more laid-back, long-stay crowd.

  • Good for: groups of friends, first-timers, nightlife, food lovers, budget travellers.
  • Trade-offs: crowded beaches near Calangute and Baga, heavy traffic in peak season, and noisier nights.

South Goa: for space and slowness

The south has longer, cleaner beaches with fewer shacks: Colva and Benaulim near Margao, Cavelossim and Mobor further down, and Palolem, Agonda and Patnem in the far south, with their bays and calm water.

  • Good for: couples, families with young children, honeymooners, anyone who wants to read on a beach.
  • Trade-offs: fewer nightlife options, longer drives between places, and resorts that can feel isolated without a car.
{{photo:goa}}

Which airport should you fly into?

Manohar International Airport at Mopa (GOX) opened in January 2023 in the far north. Dabolim (GOI) sits in south-central Goa. From Mopa, North Goa beaches like Anjuna are roughly 45 to 70 minutes away, while Palolem in the far south is a much longer drive. From Dabolim, South Goa beaches are close, and Calangute and Baga are about an hour away. Check the airport code before you book, because many people land at the wrong one for their hotel.

Can you do both?

Yes, and with five or more days it is the best way to see Goa. Spend the first half in the north and move south for the slower second half, ideally via Panaji and Old Goa's churches on the way. With only three or four days, pick one side and save the driving.

Ready-made plans: 5 days in North Goa, 5 days in South Goa, 7 days covering both, and a family-friendly 5-day plan.

{{fig:checklist}}

When to go

November to February brings the best weather and the biggest crowds and prices, especially from Christmas to New Year. March to May is hot, but quieter and cheaper. In the monsoon (June to September), many shacks close and swimming can be dangerous. It is beautiful inland, with waterfalls like Dudhsagar at their fullest, but it is not a beach holiday.

Getting around

Most visitors rent a scooter or hire a car with a driver. Carry your driving licence, and always wear a helmet, because checks are common. App cabs are more limited than in big cities, so ask your hotel about local taxi options and agree fares before you start.

Airport information was checked in November 2026. Beach conditions, shack seasons and safety flags change, so follow lifeguard flags on every beach.

title: Golden Triangle Itinerary: Delhi, Agra & Jaipur in 5 or 7 Days
quickAnswer: Five days covers Delhi, Agra and Jaipur comfortably; seven adds Old Delhi, Fatehpur Sikri and Jaipur's hill forts. Take the fast train from Delhi to Agra (about 1 hour 40 minutes), then drive to Jaipur via Fatehpur Sikri, and keep the Taj visit off Fridays.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Golden Triangle Itinerary: Delhi, Agra, Jaipur in 5–7 Days
metaDescription: A realistic Golden Triangle route for 5 or 7 days: travel times, fast trains, the Friday Taj closure, the best season and how to extend into Rajasthan.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day Delhi, Agra and Jaipur plan for your dates.

ogTitle: Golden Triangle Itinerary: Delhi, Agra & Jaipur in 5 or 7 Days
ogDescription: A realistic Golden Triangle route for 5 or 7 days: travel times, fast trains, the Friday Taj closure, the best season and how to extend into Rajasthan.
content:
Give the Golden Triangle five days if you want the highlights at a comfortable pace, and seven days if you want time for old Delhi, Fatehpur Sikri and Jaipur's forts without rushing. The usual order is Delhi → Agra → Jaipur → back to Delhi. Use the fast train from Delhi to Agra (about 1 hour 40 minutes), then drive Agra to Jaipur (about 240 km, 4.5 to 5 hours) with a stop at Fatehpur Sikri.

Delhi, Agra and Jaipur form a rough triangle, and nearly every first trip to India includes them. The circuit is simple, which is exactly why it is easy to overpack. The biggest mistake is squeezing all three cities into three days and spending half of it on the road.

{{fig:compare}}

The route and the distances

LegBest wayTypical time
Delhi → AgraFast train (Gatimaan Express or Vande Bharat) to Agra CanttAbout 1 hr 40 min by train; about 3–3.5 hrs by road via the Yamuna Expressway
Agra → JaipurCar, with a stop at Fatehpur SikriAbout 4.5–5 hrs for roughly 240 km, plus stop time
Jaipur → DelhiTrain or carAbout 4.5–5.5 hrs by train; 5–6 hrs by road

Book trains on IRCTC as soon as your dates are fixed. Morning trains to Agra sell out quickly between October and March.

The 5-day version

  1. Day 1, Delhi: Humayun's Tomb, India Gate and Qutub Minar.
  2. Day 2, Delhi to Agra: a morning train, then Agra Fort and sunset at Mehtab Bagh.
  3. Day 3, Agra to Jaipur: the Taj Mahal at opening time, then drive to Jaipur via Fatehpur Sikri.
  4. Day 4, Jaipur: Amber Fort early, then the City Palace and Hawa Mahal.
  5. Day 5, back to Delhi: bazaars in the morning, then the train or drive back.

Full day-by-day plan: Golden Triangle in 5 days.

{{photo:taj-mahal}}

What the 7-day version adds

  • A full day for Old Delhi: the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and the lanes of Chandni Chowk.
  • A relaxed afternoon at Fatehpur Sikri instead of a rushed stop.
  • A second Jaipur day for Nahargarh, Jaigarh and the old city markets.

See the 7-day Golden Triangle itinerary.

{{fig:checklist}}

Plan around the Friday closure

The Taj Mahal is closed to sightseers every Friday. Build your route so that your Agra morning falls on any other day. If your dates force a Friday in Agra, use it for Agra Fort, Mehtab Bagh and Fatehpur Sikri, and see the Taj the next morning.

When to go

October to March is the best time. Days are pleasant, but December and January mornings can be foggy, which delays some trains and hides the Taj at sunrise. April to June is very hot, and July to September is humid and rainy, but quieter and cheaper.

Extend the trip

From Jaipur, the circuit continues naturally into Rajasthan: Udaipur, Jodhpur or Jaisalmer. Our Rajasthan route planner explains which cities fit a 7 or 10-day trip.

Train times and distances were checked against railway timetables and route data in November 2026. Timetables change, so confirm on IRCTC when booking.

compare.caption: 5 days or 7 days?, side by side.

title: Rajasthan Itinerary: The Best Route for 7 or 10 Days
quickAnswer: With 7 days, do Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur, with Ranakpur on the way. With 10 days, add Jaisalmer and the Thar Desert, plus Pushkar if you like slower towns. Travel October to March and stay at least two nights per city.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Rajasthan Itinerary for 7 or 10 Days: Best Route
metaDescription: Which Rajasthan cities fit 7 or 10 days, realistic drive times between Jaipur, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Udaipur, car vs train, and the best season.

cta.ctaBody: Get a day-by-day route with realistic drive times for your dates.

ogTitle: Rajasthan Itinerary: The Best Route for 7 or 10 Days
ogDescription: Which Rajasthan cities fit 7 or 10 days, realistic drive times between Jaipur, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Udaipur, car vs train, and the best season.
content:
With 7 days in Rajasthan, pick three cities: Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur, with the Ranakpur temple on the drive between the last two. With 10 days, add Jaisalmer and the Thar Desert, and Pushkar if you like slower towns. Travel between October and March, and avoid moving cities every day: two nights per city is the minimum that feels like a holiday.

Rajasthan looks compact on a map, but the drives are long. Jaipur to Jodhpur alone is about 335 km. A good Rajasthan trip is less about how many cities you tick off and more about choosing the right ones for your days.

{{fig:compare}}

The 7-day route: the royal triangle

  1. Days 1–2, Jaipur: Amber Fort early, then the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and the bazaars of the old city.
  2. Day 3, Jaipur to Jodhpur: about 5.5 to 6 hours by road, or a train. Evening walk around the clock tower.
  3. Day 4, Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fort in the morning, then the blue lanes below it.
  4. Day 5, Jodhpur to Udaipur: via the Ranakpur Jain temple, a long but beautiful day.
  5. Days 6–7, Udaipur: the City Palace, a boat on Lake Pichola, and a day trip to Kumbhalgarh (about 84 km) if you want a fort with a view.
{{photo:jodhpur}}

The 10-day route: add the desert

Ten days lets you add Jaisalmer, the golden fort town near the Thar Desert, and Pushkar's lake and ghats:

  1. Days 1–2: Jaipur.
  2. Day 3: Pushkar, about 2.5 to 3 hours from Jaipur, via Ajmer.
  3. Days 4–5: Jodhpur.
  4. Days 6–7: Jaisalmer, about 285 km (around 5 hours) from Jodhpur. See Jaisalmer Fort, then spend a night at a desert camp near the dunes.
  5. Day 8: the long transfer towards Udaipur. Jaisalmer to Udaipur is close to 500 km by road, a full day. Leave early, or break the journey in Jodhpur.
  6. Days 9–10: Udaipur.

Day-by-day versions: Rajasthan in 10 days, 2 days in Jaisalmer, 2 days in Udaipur and 4 days in Mewar.

{{fig:checklist}}

Car with driver, or trains?

  • Car with driver: the most common choice. It lets you stop at Ranakpur, Kumbhalgarh or small villages on the way, and doors open where you need them. Agree on the route, the number of days and what is included (tolls, parking, driver's stay) in writing.
  • Trains: good on the Jaipur–Jodhpur and Jodhpur–Jaisalmer legs, and cheaper for solo travellers. They do not help with Ranakpur or Kumbhalgarh, which need road transport.
  • A mix: trains for the long straight legs, and a car for the scenic Jodhpur–Udaipur day.

When to go

October to March is the comfortable season. December and January nights in the desert get very cold, so pack a warm layer for camps. From April to June, daytime heat in Jaisalmer and Jodhpur is extreme. The monsoon, July to September, makes Udaipur green and lovely, but the desert dusty and humid.

Starting from Delhi?

Add Agra at the start with the Golden Triangle, then continue from Jaipur into this route. Keep at least 9 or 10 days for that combined trip.

Distances and drive times are typical road estimates, checked in November 2026. Real times depend on traffic, stops and road works.

compare.caption: 7 days or 10 days?, side by side.

title: Best Places to Visit in India in December (2026)
quickAnswer: December's best picks are Goa, Kerala, the Rann of Kutch during Rann Utsav, Rajasthan, the Andaman Islands, Hampi, Gulmarg for snow and Nagaland's Hornbill Festival. It is peak season, so book flights, trains and stays early, especially around Christmas and New Year.
author: VacayOut Editors / India travel desk
metaTitle: Best Places to Visit in India in December 2026
metaDescription: 8 places in India that are at their best in December, from the Rann Utsav and Goa to Kerala, Hampi and Gulmarg, with the catch for each and when to book.
focusKeyword: best places to visit in india in december

cta.ctaBody: Tell the AI planner your days and interests, and get a plan.

ogTitle: Best Places to Visit in India in December (2026)
ogDescription: 8 places in India that are at their best in December, from the Rann Utsav and Goa to Kerala, Hampi and Gulmarg, with the catch for each and when to book.
content:
December is one of the best months to travel in India. The south and the coasts are dry and warm, the desert is cool, and the Himalaya has its first snow. The top picks are Goa, Kerala, the Rann of Kutch during Rann Utsav, Rajasthan, the Andaman Islands, Hampi, and Gulmarg for snow. December is also peak season, so book flights, trains and stays early, especially for Christmas and New Year.

The right December trip depends on what you want: sun, snow, festivals or heritage. Here are the destinations that are genuinely at their best this month, with the catch for each, so you can choose with your eyes open.

{{fig:facts}}

1. Rann of Kutch, Gujarat: for the white desert

The salt flats of the Rann of Kutch are at their most striking in winter. Rann Utsav's tent city at Dhordo runs from 1 November 2026 to 7 March 2027, and the December full-moon period (around 22 to 24 December) is the most sought-after time, according to Outlook Traveller. Bhuj is the gateway. The catch: full-moon dates book out early, and you need a permit to enter the White Rann, so check whether your package includes it.

2. Goa: for beaches, food and Christmas

Goa has dry, sunny weather in December and a festive Christmas and New Year atmosphere. Choose your side with our North vs South Goa guide. The catch: prices jump in the last ten days of the year, so book early or travel in the first half of the month.

{{photo:rann-of-kutch}}

3. Kerala: for backwaters and hills

After the monsoon, Kerala is green, the houseboat season is in full swing and Munnar's tea hills are cool and clear. Read our houseboat guide before booking. The catch: the Christmas week is busy and houseboats sell out.

4. Rajasthan: for forts and the desert

Warm days and cold nights make December ideal for Rajasthan's forts and for a desert camp near Jaisalmer. Plan your route with our 7 or 10-day Rajasthan guide. The catch: desert nights get close to freezing, so pack warm layers.

5. Andaman Islands: for clear water

December has calm seas and good visibility for snorkelling and diving around Havelock and Neil. Read our ferry guide first. The catch: ferries and island hotels fill up fast in December, so book them before anything else.

6. Hampi, Karnataka: for ruins without the heat

The boulder landscape and temples of Hampi are best explored when it is cool. December mornings are perfect for cycling between the ruins. See our 3-day Hampi itinerary. The catch: afternoons are still warm, so start early.

7. Gulmarg, Kashmir: for the first snow

Snow usually settles in Gulmarg through December, and the ski season builds towards January. Read our Gulmarg winter guide for gondola booking. The catch: heavy snow in December varies from year to year, so stay flexible.

8. Nagaland: for the Hornbill Festival

The Hornbill Festival at Kisama Heritage Village, near Kohima, is listed for 1 to 10 December 2026. It brings together the music, dance, crafts and food of Nagaland's communities. Pair it with our 5-day Nagaland itinerary. The catch: Kohima's hotels fill fast during the festival, so book early.

{{fig:checklist}}

Where not to go in December

Unless you are an experienced winter traveller, skip the high Himalaya beyond the snow line, such as Ladakh and Spiti. Roads close and temperatures fall far below zero. Expect thick fog in the northern plains, including Delhi, Agra and Varanasi, which can delay early-morning trains and flights. Keep buffer time on travel days.

Plan it in minutes

Not sure which one fits your dates and budget? Tell our AI planner how many days you have and what you like. It suggests destinations and builds a day-by-day plan from our reviewed guides.

Festival dates were checked against official and news sources in November 2026. Confirm event dates with the organisers before booking.
